structural_alert_screening.why: Structural alerts (toxicophores) are molecular substructures associated with mutagenicity (e.g., aromatic amines, nitro groups, alkylating agents, epoxides). A validated set of 29 toxicophores classified mutagenicity with 82% total accuracy.

expert_system_prediction.value_or_range: Derek Nexus, Leadscope, or CASE Ultra; use consensus of rule-based + statistical approaches
expert_system_prediction.when: Regulatory-grade mutagenicity prediction per ICH M7 guidance for impurity assessment
expert_system_prediction.why: ICH M7 requires two complementary in silico methods - one expert rule-based (e.g., Derek Nexus) and one statistical/QSAR-based (e.g., CASE Ultra). Both must predict negative for a compound to be classified as non-mutagenic without experimental testing.

machine_learning_models.value_or_range: Random Forest, SVM, or deep learning models; typical AUC 0.85-0.90 on benchmark datasets
machine_learning_models.when: High-throughput screening of large compound libraries for mutagenic liability
machine_learning_models.why: ML models trained on the Hansen benchmark dataset (>6,500 compounds) achieve AUC of 0.85-0.90. Models using molecular fingerprints (ECFP6) combined with physicochemical descriptors generally outperform those using either alone.

common_mistakes: Using a single prediction method when ICH M7 requires two complementary methods
Not distinguishing between alerting structures that cause mutagenicity via different mechanisms (direct-acting vs. requiring metabolic activation)
Ignoring that many structural alerts have high false positive rates and require expert interpretation

hepatotoxicity_prediction.description: Prediction of drug-induced liver injury (DILI), which is the leading cause of post-market drug withdrawals. Includes both intrinsic (dose-dependent) and idiosyncratic (unpredictable) hepatotoxicity.

dili_risk_assessment.value_or_range: Binary classification (DILI-positive vs DILI-negative); best models achieve ~71% accuracy with ECFP6 fingerprints
dili_risk_assessment.when: Early assessment of hepatotoxicity risk for drug candidates
dili_risk_assessment.why: DILI accounts for 18% of drug withdrawals. Early prediction allows design-out of hepatotoxic liability. Ensemble models combining molecular fingerprints with deep neural networks and traditional ML achieve the best performance.

daily_dose_and_lipophilicity_rule.value_or_range: Daily dose > 100 mg AND LogP > 3: significantly elevated DILI risk
daily_dose_and_lipophilicity_rule.when: Quick risk stratification based on simple physicochemical and dosing properties
daily_dose_and_lipophilicity_rule.why: The '2-out-of-3 rule' (daily dose > 100 mg, LogP > 3, metabolism by CYPs) identifies compounds with significantly elevated DILI risk. This simple rule provides rapid risk stratification before more complex predictions.

reactive_metabolite_assessment.value_or_range: Screen for bioactivation-prone functional groups (furans, thiophenes, anilines, hydrazines)
reactive_metabolite_assessment.when: Evaluating mechanism-based hepatotoxicity risk from reactive metabolites
reactive_metabolite_assessment.why: Many DILI cases are caused by reactive metabolites that form covalent adducts with cellular proteins (especially CYP-mediated bioactivation). Identifying bioactivation-prone substructures is a key component of hepatotoxicity risk assessment.

common_mistakes: Treating DILI prediction as a solved problem when even the best models have ~30% error rates
Not considering dose as a critical factor (most DILI occurs at daily doses > 100 mg)
Ignoring reactive metabolite formation as a mechanism of DILI
Using single-endpoint models when DILI involves multiple mechanisms (mitochondrial toxicity, bile salt transport inhibition, immune-mediated injury)

toxicity_prediction.best_practice_notes: Use multiple complementary toxicity prediction methods and take a consensus. For Ames mutagenicity, follow ICH M7 guidance requiring two complementary in silico methods (expert rule-based + statistical). For DILI prediction, consider both structural alerts for reactive metabolites and physicochemical/dose-based rules. Always validate computational predictions experimentally for lead compounds. Consider dose-dependent vs. idiosyncratic toxicity mechanisms separately. LD50 predictions are most reliable for acute toxicity; chronic toxicity (NOAEL) predictions have much higher uncertainty.
